html:
The system of forced rubber collection in the Congo Free State, the private colony of King Leopold II of Belgium from 1885 to 1908, and one of the worst colonial atrocities.

The powers at the Berlin Conference accepted Leopold's claim to the Congo basin. When the bicycle and car tyre made rubber valuable in the 1890s, his state and the companies it licensed forced villages to collect wild rubber to fixed quotas. The army, the Force Publique, took women hostage, burned villages and killed those who fell short. Soldiers cut off hands to prove they had used their bullets on people.

Deaths from killing, famine, disease and falling birth rates ran into the millions, though no one can give an exact number. Missionaries, the journalist E. D. Morel and the British consul Roger Casement exposed the abuses, and the Congo Reform Association took them worldwide. In 1908 Belgium took the colony from the king as the Belgian Congo. A similar rubber terror ran in the Amazon.
sum: The system of forced rubber collection in the Congo Free State, the private colony of King Leopold II of Belgium from 1885 to 1908, and one of the worst colonial atrocities.
